summary: Eighty generations of doubling release the energy, almost all of it in the last few.

paragraphs.text: At peak squeeze the crushed initiator releases a burst of neutrons. One strikes a plutonium nucleus, which wobbles, necks and splits into two fragments. Each fission releases {{mev_per_fission}} and frees {{neutrons_per_fission}} new neutrons.

Each new neutron can split another nucleus, so the number of fissions roughly doubles with every generation. A generation lasts {{generation_time}}. The tracks drawn here are only the first few generations. After that there are too many, so they are shown as a glowing density.

The doubling runs for {{generations}} generations. For most of that time the energy released is still tiny, so almost nothing seems to happen. Clean doubling is a simplification, drawn here for illustration.
Doubling is sudden at the end. The last few generations release nearly all of the energy, and the core heats to {{core_temp}}. The total is {{yield_j}}.

events.detail: The crushed initiator releases a burst of neutrons at maximum compression, and the first fissions begin.
After about ten generations there are too many neutron paths to draw one by one.
The final few generations release nearly all of the energy.

callouts.text: A burst of neutrons from the initiator starts the chain.
Too many paths to draw one by one. From here the neutrons are shown as a glowing density.
For most of this microsecond almost nothing seems to happen.
The last few doublings release almost all of the energy.
